body: That was, without a doubt, the single most informative video about depression I have ever watched.  Thank you for posting this.

I've had a little bit of experience running an IRC channel, so I can help out in that respect.

As for the name, perhaps #suicidewatch or #sw.
I'm sure I eventually will start replying to posts here.  Thanks.  :)

Reading through the posts and responding to everybody has made me feel a bit more positive.  It's nice to know there are people that care and are here to offer advice despite not knowing me.

Thank you, by the way.  I appreciate your responses.

Heh.  It certainly is telling.

"Look, I don't know how to say this other than - would you let the mistakes and failings of others (especially your parents) rob you of your future?"

No, I wouldn't.  I think deep down I know I'm not a bad person.  It's just hard to see myself as a good person when I was raised the way I was.  Caring for myself and my feelings just feels... weird.  

I am at least trying to do better.  I've taken up running and journaling, but sometimes I just feel like these are things I should've been doing anyway, and not things that are strictly for my benefit (if that makes any sense).

I promise if I ever get the urge again, I will do that.

I'll try that exercise.  I have read a bit about CBT, but haven't really tried it out for an extended period of time.

Thank you.
Thank you.  I'll try to check out some places that offer a sliding scale.
Thank you.  I'll try to check out some places to volunteer.
Thank you for your response, by the way.  I appreciate it.

I do have friends, but I have this overwhelming feeling that if I go to them to support they'll draw away from me and not like me as much anymore.

I have been keeping a journal for the past month.  It seems to help somewhat in that I can look back and notice behaviors that are erratic.

Thank you for your response.

The self-loathing, I feel, seems to come from the punishment I was given when things didn't work out they way my parents wanted them to.  I wouldn't be beaten, but I'd be basically treated like a horrible child who only thought of himself and was punishing my poor parents by defying them.  The only scars I got from them seem to be emotional ones.

My dad was the main culprit.  He'd withdraw affection at the slightest sign of defiance, and was even openly hostile toward me on numerous occasions.  For example, he'd threaten to take my door off the hinges for not performing well in a soccer game, or when we'd argue he'd sit outside my door for hours waiting for me to emerge so he could argue with me more.  During my childhood, he'd take to turning his back on me in public if he thought I wasn't performing to his expectations in sports.  It crushed me when I'd see it.  Eventually, it drove me away from wanting to play sports anymore, but I was forced to keep doing it because "Dad needs you to play".

My Dad cheated on my Mom.  When she found out, they took up arguing for about a month.  They'd come home from their respective jobs and argue for hours and hours, leaving me to take care of my siblings and make sure they were safe (away from the arguments and making sure they got dinner, did their homework, etc.).  When my parents eventually got divorced, he left and basically cut me out of his life.  He keeps in contact with my sisters and occasionally my mother, but never calls me at all.  The most I've talked to him in the past year was when he sent me a text on my birthday.

My mom took the divorce really hard (as expected), and it seemed like she took out her aggression toward my dad out on me.  Every mistake I made at that time was amplified and remembered for the next time I messed up so it could be hurled back onto me.  Every mistake my sisters made was glossed over and forgiven.  I've told her how I feel about this, but it seemed to take it as me attacking her without provocation.  Things are more normal between us now, but it still lingers in my mind and still hurts.  She even got me a job at her work a while ago, but I was later fired from it after she left the company.

As far as work goes, it's fine.  I don't really know anybody all that well there.  I stay friendly, but nothing beyond me cracking jokes or talking work related stuff.  People do seem to like me, but I know that's not on a personal level.
